user.title: Connect your Govee account
user.description: Get an API key in the Govee Home app: Profile → Settings → Apply for API Key. Govee emails it to you.

data_description.scan_interval: How often to ask Govee for the lamp's state. Govee allows about 10,000 requests a day per key, so keep this at 60 seconds or more if you have several lamps.
data_description.use_lan: Faster and local, and doesn't count against the daily limit. Turn on "LAN Control" for the lamp in the Govee app first. Segment lights still use the cloud.
data_description.lan_hosts: Only needed if lamps aren't found automatically, for example when Home Assistant runs in Docker without host networking. Separate addresses with commas.

devices.title: Choose your lamps
devices.description: Found {count} Govee lights. Lamps with more than one light are preselected.

reauth_confirm.title: Govee API key expired
reauth_confirm.description: Govee rejected the stored API key. Paste a new one.

error.invalid_auth: Govee rejected this API key. Check for missing characters, or request a new key in the Govee app.
error.cannot_connect: Couldn't reach Govee's servers. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.no_devices: This Govee account has no lights.

abort.already_configured: This Govee account is already set up.

menu_options.pick_lamp: Map a lamp's lights to segments

zones.title: Lights in {name}
zones.description:
This lamp reports {count} segments, numbered 0 to {last}.

**Main light + ring**: the lamp's own controls drive the main light, and the lights below are made of segments (usually the ring).
**LAN sections**: each light is a section number (1, 2, 3 …) switched with local LAN commands. Try this if the ring doesn't react to *Main light + ring*. Needs LAN Control. Put the section number in the segments field, for example Main = `1`, Ring = `2`.
**Split segments into lights**: every light is a run of segments. Good for floor lamps.

Leave a row empty to skip it. To switch layout and get its default rows, choose the layout and tick *Reset*.

data.reset: Reset rows to the default for this layout

error.incomplete: Give this light both a name and segments.
error.bad_segments: Use segment numbers within the lamp's range, like 0-9 or 3, 5, 7.
error.overlap: These segments are already used by another light.
error.bad_section: Use a single section number from 1 to 9.
error.no_segments: This lamp reports no segments. Choose the LAN sections layout instead.

abort.cannot_connect: Couldn't reach Govee's servers. Try again in a moment.
abort.no_segment_lamps: No lamps are selected. Add one under Lamps and refresh interval first.

set_segments.name: Set segments
set_segments.description: Paint individual segments of a Govee lamp. Use it to find out which segments belong to which light.

rgb_color.name: Colour
rgb_color.description: Colour to paint. Defaults to red.

send_lan_frames.name: Send LAN frames
send_lan_frames.description: Send raw Govee command frames to a lamp over LAN. The checksum is added for you. For finding out which commands a lamp understands.

frames.name: Frames
frames.description: List of frames in hex, like ["33 30 02 00"].

lan_not_found.title: {name} not found on your network
lan_not_found.description:
The LAN sections layout controls {name} over your local network, but the lamp didn't answer. Its lights stay unavailable until it's found.

1. In the Govee app, open the lamp's settings and check that **LAN Control** is on.
2. Make sure Home Assistant and the lamp are on the same network (no guest Wi-Fi, no VLAN in between). In Docker, Home Assistant needs host networking.
3. Remove the built-in **Govee lights local** integration if it's set up. Only one integration can receive Govee LAN replies.
4. Give the lamp a fixed IP address in your router and enter it under **Undumb Govee → Configure → Lamps and refresh interval → Lamp IP addresses**.

This message disappears by itself once the lamp is found.
